records.name: Ministry of Awe
records.summary: An immersive art space in a former bank building on 3rd Street, where visitors walk through rooms of art. You buy a timed ticket to visit, and the group also offers a membership and a mailing list.
records.what_you_do: Visit the art rooms during open hours with a timed ticket. Join the mailing list or the membership to support the space.

schedule.text: Open Wednesday and Thursday 11 am to 6 pm, Friday 11 am to 10 pm, Saturday 11 am to 9 pm, Sunday 10 am to 6 pm, closed Monday and Tuesday. The visit page says events begin September 1 with no year given.

cost.text: Ticketed. Prices are not listed on the visit page. Children's tickets exist; children under 2 are free.

first_step.how: Buy a timed entry ticket through the BUY TICKETS link on moaphilly.org, and book ahead to skip the wait
first_step.basis: Open to the public with tickets sold online; walk-up entry depends on availability

records.notes: Site has a working schedule and ticket link but no dated news. The home page says 'Tickets Available Soon' and 'OPEN NOW' at once, and the visit page says tickets are not yet on sale; the opening date has no year. Social links (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok) were seen but not recorded because no exact URLs were captured. Membership details are not shown.

records.name: Movimiento Administradores de Arte en Pensilvania (MAAP)
records.summary: A group that helps artists of color get fair access to arts space and grant money. It runs online workshops and offers booked advising sessions on grant applications.
records.what_you_do: Join an online workshop to learn where to find arts resources and meet other artists. Book an advising session for help with a grant application.

schedule.text: Online workshops and grant advising by appointment. No fixed weekly schedule is listed.

cost.text: A free introduction session is listed. Workshop and advising fees are not shown.

first_step.how: Book the introduction session through the 'Reservar cita' link on maapensilvania.org, or sign up for an online workshop
first_step.basis: Public workshops and booked advising are open to artists; the site names BIPOC artists as its focus

records.notes: Working site with no dated posts. Its focus is 'BIPOC individuals and communities', so the community tags were left empty rather than guessed. Its tag is 'racial_equity' because no arts access tag fits. The site lists CultureWorks as its address, so CultureWorks is a lead.

records.name: Music Theatre Philly
records.summary: A nonprofit theater school and production group that teaches singing, acting, and dance. Classes run for ages 2 and up, and it stages fall shows for students.
records.what_you_do: Take a class in singing, acting, or dance, or try a private lesson. Students can also audition for the fall shows.

schedule.text: Classes for ages 2 to adult, with a class finder page. Spring 2027 classes are advertised. Fall productions are staged for grades 1 to 12.

cost.text: Class fees are not shown on the page. Scholarships and donations are offered.

first_step.how: Use the 'Which class is for you?' page to pick a class, then call 445-223-2683 or use the contact form
first_step.basis: Classes are open to beginners at every age, and the site has a page that helps new students choose

records.notes: Spring 2027 classes are advertised. The site also mentions a 2026 award with no month. The Playhouse play space for ages 6 months to 5 years and birthday parties are also offered. MTP Players is a separate group name on the site and was not recorded separately. The phone number is recorded as published.

records.name: Musicopia
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that brings music and dance to schools and communities through workshops, short residencies, lessons, and student ensembles.
records.what_you_do: Take part in a workshop or residency, or join a student ensemble or lessons program. Volunteers and donors can also help.

schedule.text: Programs are set up with schools and partners. No public class schedule is listed.

first_step.how: Email info@musicopia.org or call (215) 829-9522 to ask about lessons, a residency, or volunteering
first_step.basis: Most programs run through schools and partners, and the public way in is not spelled out

records.notes: The musicopia.net address redirects to musicopia.org. A Lullaby concert is mentioned in a testimonial with no date. A volunteer page is linked but has no details. The site names no public class schedule, so the status rests on a working site with no dated posts.

schedule.text: No current show or class is listed on the site

records.what_you_do: Watch a public performance, or ask about classes. The site says it offers classes in all parts of Chinese opera but does not list enrollment steps.

schedule.text: Upcoming events are to be announced. Past performances were held at the Penn Museum, the Free Library, and at Mid-Autumn Festival events.

cost.text: No class fees are listed. Some past shows were free.

first_step.how: Watch the Events and Media page for the next performance, or use the contact page to ask about classes
first_step.basis: Classes are mentioned, but the site does not publish how to enroll

records.notes: Newest dated item is a Penn Museum performance on 2023-01-21, which makes the status dormant. The site lists a 2023 arts award and 2022 and 2021 online performances. Asian Americans United is named as an organizer and is a lead.
